meta.name: RPSGT Visual Skills Pack 2 — neighboring-epoch evidence
meta.sourceBasis: Five 90-second teaching sequences reuse original Sleep Pathways Guild 30-second W, N1, N2, N3, and REM schematic epochs to practice visual recognition across neighboring context.
meta.clinicalBoundary: Sequence order is pedagogic and does not imply mandatory sleep architecture. Real staging requires the current official scoring criteria, the complete recording, facility procedures, and supervised scorer training.

cases.title: Brief wake-oriented context
cases.stagePrompt: Which stage is the center 30-second teaching epoch designed to represent?
cases.channelPrompt: Which displayed channel best demonstrates the posterior alpha teaching clue in the center epoch?

evidence.prompt: Click one prominent eye-blink teaching deflection in E1-M2 within the center epoch.
evidence.rationale: The center teaching epoch combines posterior alpha with wake-oriented eye activity and relatively higher chin tone.

cases.title: Wake-to-light-sleep context
cases.stagePrompt: Which stage is the center 30-second teaching epoch designed to represent?
cases.channelPrompt: Which displayed channel best demonstrates the slow-eye-movement teaching clue in the center epoch?

evidence.prompt: Click the vertex-wave teaching feature in C3-M2 within the center epoch.
evidence.rationale: The center teaching epoch emphasizes a light-sleep background, slow eye movements, and a vertex teaching feature without the N2 teaching markers used in the next epoch.

cases.title: Light-to-deeper NREM context
cases.stagePrompt: Which stage is the center 30-second teaching epoch designed to represent?
cases.channelPrompt: Which displayed channel carries the clearest spindle and K-complex teaching morphology in the center epoch?

evidence.prompt: Mark the spindle teaching burst from beginning to end in C3-M2 within the center epoch.
evidence.rationale: The center teaching epoch contains the spindle/K-complex morphology used to distinguish this schematic N2 example from its neighboring N1 and N3 examples.

cases.title: Deep NREM context
cases.stagePrompt: Which stage is the center 30-second teaching epoch designed to represent?
cases.channelPrompt: Which displayed channel best demonstrates the large frontal slow-wave teaching activity in the center epoch?

evidence.prompt: Mark the first sustained slow-wave teaching run in F3-M2 within the center epoch.
evidence.rationale: The center teaching epoch emphasizes large frontal slow-wave activity compared with the lighter N2 examples on both sides.

cases.title: REM-to-awakening context
cases.stagePrompt: Which stage is the center 30-second teaching epoch designed to represent?
cases.channelPrompt: Which displayed channel best demonstrates the rapid-eye-movement teaching clue in the center epoch?

evidence.prompt: Mark the rapid-eye-movement teaching burst in E1-M2 within the center epoch.
evidence.rationale: The center teaching epoch combines rapid eye movements with a REM-oriented EEG background and low chin tone before the neighboring wake example.
